stories.title: Pladis Appoints Frankgerald Stepp as Chief Supply Chain Officer
summary: Global snacking company Pladis has appointed Frankgerald Stepp as its chief supply chain officer. Stepp, a former executive at Kerry Group, will officially assume the role in January 2027. He succeeds Mario Reis, who is scheduled to retire at the end of December 2026 after nearly ten years with the business. In his new capacity, Stepp will oversee Pladis' operations spanning across more than 110 international markets.

The leadership change follows significant capital investments by Pladis aimed at strengthening production capacity, improving operational efficiency, and building supply chain resilience. In 2025, the company—whose portfolio includes brands such as McVitie’s, Ülker, and Godiva—invested more than £100 million in capital expenditure. This funding supported network reliability, including a £68 million investment in UK bakeries, facility expansions in Cairo, and operational enhancements in France, Türkiye, and the United States.

Stepp brings extensive industry experience to Pladis, having recently served as chief operations officer of Kerry Group's biotechnology business and global vice-president of manufacturing. His previous background includes leadership positions at ARYZTA, Kraft Foods, and Mondelez International. Pladis Chief Human Resources Officer Geraldine Fraser credited outgoing officer Reis with establishing a strong operational foundation and highlighted Stepp's baking industry expertise as critical for supporting the company's future growth strategy.

stories.title: Reckitt Outlines Strategy for North American Growth at Investor Seminar
summary: Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC hosted its latest investor seminar, titled "Reckitt Focus On: North America," to share insights into the company's regional business, strategy, and primary growth drivers. The event provided investors and analysts with a detailed look at the North American market's role in supporting Reckitt's long-term growth objectives.

The seminar was led by Jérôme Lemaire, President of North America, who was joined by Chief Financial Officer Shannon Eisenhardt and VP of Customer Marketing for North America Jonathan Weiss. Discussions focused on the region's brand portfolio, sales and omnichannel capabilities, and the investments made into building a local supply network.

According to the company, no new material financial or trading information was scheduled for disclosure during the event. The seminar was made accessible to participants via a live stream hosted on Reckitt's corporate website.

stories.title: Reckitt Finalizes Sale of Russia Hygiene Division to Arnest Management LLC
summary: Reckitt Benckiser Group plc announced on 12 November 2026 that it has completed the divestment of its Russia Hygiene business to Arnest Management LLC after receiving all required regulatory approvals. The transaction, initially disclosed on 24 July 2026, is part of Reckitt's ongoing strategy to simplify its global portfolio and reshape its geographic footprint. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

Following Reckitt's Alternative Performance Measure policies regarding disposals, the Russia Hygiene segment has been excluded from the company's Like-for-Like (LFL) Net Revenue growth metrics. Restated figures for Q3 2026 indicate LFL Net Revenue growth of 9.8% in Emerging Markets, 3.9% for Core Reckitt, and 3.8% for Core Reckitt plus MJN. For the year-to-date period through Q3 2026, restated LFL growth stood at 10.2% for Emerging Markets, 3.5% for Core Reckitt, and 3.4% for Core Reckitt plus MJN.

Reckitt confirmed that the completed transaction is not expected to materially impact its Group Adjusted Operating Profit or Adjusted EPS for 2026. The company employs approximately 36,000 people worldwide and distributes around 30 million products daily across more than 80 countries, operating in business segments such as Germ Protection, Household Care, Intimate Wellness, and Self Care.

stories.title: Reckitt Stock Valuation Analysis Indicates Potential Undervaluation Relative to Future Cash Flows
summary: Reckitt Benckiser Group (LSE:RKT) has achieved a 23.2% return over the past three years, with its share price trading around £57.78. Over the latest twelve-month period, the company produced approximately £2.17 billion in free cash flow, driven by its core business of converting branded household and consumer health sales into cash generation.

A Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) evaluation indicates that the intrinsic value of the business lies significantly above its current market price of £57.78, suggesting the stock may be 32% undervalued based on cash flow. Analyst forecasts feeding into the DCF model project that Reckitt's free cash flow will stay in the billions of pounds and grow from its current base into the early 2030s.

Complementing the cash flow assessment, an analyst consensus narrative on Simply Wall St estimates the stock is 8% undervalued based on revenue and earnings metrics. This consensus highlights the ongoing execution of Reckitt's Fuel for Growth programme, which aims to bring operating overheads below 19% of net revenue by the end of 2027.

stories.title: pladis Launches Second Global Accelerator Programme Targeting Sustainable Nutrition and Ingredient Innovation
summary: Global snacking group pladis, the company behind brands including McVitie’s and Godiva, has launched its second global accelerator programme to collaborate with innovative food-tech start-ups. The initiative focuses on improving product nutrition and developing sustainable solutions in response to rising GLP-1 medication adoption and climate-related supply chain disruptions. Up to 12 selected start-ups will receive technical and operational guidance from pladis experts, with three to six candidates potentially progressing to pilot or co-development phases.

Participation in the programme is free, with applications open until January 15 and operations commencing in March. Pladis is targeting key innovation areas, including fermentation, enzymatic processing, sensory science, natural alternatives to additives, gut health, and functional ingredients. The initiative also seeks to solve challenges surrounding ingredient supply resilience, particularly regarding cocoa crops impacted by adverse weather conditions and disease.

The launch follows an initial accelerator scheme that engaged 12 start-ups supported by 37 mentors across pladis and Yıldız Holding. Technologies highlighted from the prior cohort included Zya's enzyme designed to convert sugar into fiber post-consumption, Fermtech's fermentation method converting food-industry by-products into a cocoa alternative, and Nuritas's use of artificial intelligence to identify bioactive plant peptides for functional food ingredients.

stories.title: Pladis Expands China Market Presence with McVitie’s Flipz Pretzels Launch
summary: London-based snack manufacturer Pladis has launched McVitie's-branded Flipz pretzels in China as part of a strategy to expand its portfolio beyond biscuits and chocolate. The company identified China as one of its largest long-term growth opportunities for McVitie's as it aims to scale the brand into a £1bn ($1.35bn) global entity.

Chief Commercial Officer David Murray stated that the brand's future growth will rely on expanding into broader snacking categories and introducing new product formats to reach new consumers. Pladis currently sells Godiva chocolate and McVitie's biscuits in China, following a market diversification model similar to its deployments in Saudi Arabia and Egypt with products like McVitie's Joy.

A spokesperson for Pladis confirmed a multi-million-pound investment to support the brand's development in China, focusing on manufacturing, distribution, product development, e-commerce, and brand-building. The pretzel products debuted in August, though Pladis declined to share sales forecasts or current revenue figures.

stories.title: McVitie’s owner pladis grows revenue to £3.3bn as branded portfolio proves resilient
summary: Global snacking company pladis published its Annual Report for the year ended December 31, 2025, reporting a 1.2% increase in revenue to £3.272 billion, compared with £3.232 billion in 2024. Branded sales represented approximately 90% of total revenue. Facing an environment shaped by commodity inflation, currency volatility, and macroeconomic headwinds, the company recorded an EBITDA of £473.7 million (down from £494.5 million in 2024) and an operating profit of £301.6 million (down from £344.4 million). Higher working capital requirements impacted cash generation, leaving net debt at £1.028 billion at year end.

During 2025, pladis allocated £100.5 million in capital expenditure to enhance capacity, productivity, efficiency, and operational resilience. The company simplified its manufacturing footprint in the Americas and progressed several multi-year facility investments. These included a £68 million programme across UK bakeries producing brands such as McVitie’s, Jacob’s, and Carr’s, an investment in its Cairo facility that reached £8.6 million by the end of 2025, and a €5.4 million investment in a new Mini BN line in Vertou, France.

Innovation and commercial expansion continued across key geographic markets. Products launched over the previous three years accounted for 12% of Ülker’s annual snacking revenue in Türkiye in 2025, while pladis selected 12 start-ups for its first global Accelerator Programme and progressed plans for McVitie’s expansion in China. Additionally, pladis developed its new global sustainability strategy, titled 'Happy People, Happy Planet', during 2025. Launched in April 2026, the framework targets five areas: colleagues and communities, responsible snacking, carbon, packaging and waste, and responsible sourcing.

stories.title: pladis opens applications to second year of Global Accelerator Programme

Selected participants will explore innovations in areas such as gut health, functional ingredients, personalized nutrition, enzymatic processing, fermentation, sensory science, and natural alternatives to additives. stories.title: Reckitt Cuts Annual Sales Forecast Following Lysol Supply Disruptions
summary: Reckitt lowered its annual core sales-growth forecast on October 27, 2026, due to manufacturing constraints that disrupted Lysol product supplies in North America. Following the update, Reckitt shares fell 7.1% in early trading as quarterly growth missed the 3.6% expectation from a company-compiled analyst poll. Chief Executive Kris Licht stated that while consumer demand for Lysol remained strong, the temporary manufacturing issues prevented the company from fully satisfying order volumes.

The company also cited slower growth within China's vitamins, minerals, and supplements category as a factor impacting performance. Conversely, emerging-market like-for-like revenue expanded by 8%, while Europe returned to growth at 0.8%. Reckitt's management expects North America and Lysol performance to rebound in the fourth quarter as the manufacturing problems are resolved.

To support its operations, Reckitt highlighted a multi-year U.S. investment of up to $600 million announced in September, which aims to strengthen regional supply resilience, accelerate innovation, and expand healthcare product access. The lowered outlook reverses the stance from Reckitt's July half-year report, which had retained annual growth targets supported by a 4.2% core like-for-like second-quarter growth rate.
